data.long_meaning: Sulendra is a Sanskrit and Hindu name that means 'Sun God'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Surya', which is the name of the Hindu Sun God. This name is believed to bring warmth, energy, and vitality to those who bear it. The name Sulendra carries the meaning “Sun God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sulendra usually hope their child will grow to embody sun god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Sulendra belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun God.”

historical_references.reference: Sulendra Chalukya, also known as Sulivara Chalukya, was a Chalukya king who ruled in the Karnataka region of India from 1156 to 1183 AD. He was a powerful monarch who expanded his territories through military conquests. Sulendra is known for his great patronage of Jainism, and his capital city, Halebidu, is famous for its magnificent temples.

Sulendra, also known as Sulabha, was a legendary queen of the ancient Indian Mahabharata epic. She was the wife of Bhima, one of the five Pandava brothers. Sulendra is known for her great beauty and her devotion to her husband. According to the epic, Sulendra was abducted by the demon Bakasura, but was rescued by Bhima with the help of the god Krishna.
